headlines.title: Woman dies after hit-and-run crash in San Jose
headlines.description: A woman died following a hit-and-run crash in San Jose Thursday night, according to the police department. San Jose police said officers responded to a report of a hit-and-run crash involving a pedestrian in the area of Rigoletto Drive and King Road just before 9 p.m. A woman was taken to the hospital, where she later died, authorities said. Police said the investigation is ongoing.

headlines.title: Former San Francisco immigration judge files federal whistleblower lawsuit over firing
headlines.description: A former San Francisco immigration judge fired by the Trump administration last year filed a federal whistleblower lawsuit Thursday accusing the Department of Justice of terminating her for raising due process concerns over new policy directives and ICE enforcement tactics. Judge Chloe Dillon is among 14 San Francisco judges fired since President Trump’s return to office and is the first of the group to sue over her removal. Her lawsuit opens with a quote from George Orwell: “If liberty means anything at all, it means the right to tell people what they do not want to hear.” Dillon, like dozens of other immigration judges fired since last year, was originally appointed by the Biden administration. She first took the bench in 2022 after serving for nearly a decade as a federal public defender in San Diego. “I was really excited,” Dillon told NBC Bay Area. “I felt like it was an excellent fit for me. I felt it was something that I cared about – ensuring justice in immigration court.” Over the next three years working as a judge at one of the country’s busiest immigration courts, Dillon said she resolved thousands of cases, earning excellent performance reviews along the way. According to Dillon’s lawsuit, her “decisions were almost never appealed.” “It was really interesting work,” Dillon said. “I felt like it was really important that people were heard and that their cases were decided carefully and based on all the evidence.” But Dillon said the job began to change almost immediately following President Trump’s inauguration, as new appointees took over the senior levels of the country’s immigration court system. In the spring of 2025, Dillon’s suit alleges that San Francisco Assistant Chief Immigration Judge Loi McCleskey directed the court’s judges “to grant any and all motions to change venue” filed by ICE attorneys. That meant immigrants’ cases would be transferred out of San Francisco to another court – potentially far away from their attorneys and witnesses. “I think my first reaction was confusion because I felt that the policy was not in accordance with what the law was,” Dillon said. “It was certainly part of a larger project to detain people and bring their cases to conclusion, likely resulting in deportation, as quickly as possible. Because these cases were being moved to detained courts and being moved to locations that were more remote.” Dillon’s suit alleges she expressed concern over the new directive in an email to McCleskey and later met with her supervisor in person. “ACIJ McCleskey expressed empathy with Plaintiff’s point of view but warned her that the ‘White House’ was paying attention to this and to be careful about pushing the issue further,” the lawsuit alleges. McCleskey did not immediately respond to NBC Bay Area’s request for comment. In one case, according to the suit, Dillon denied an ICE motion to change venue, but learned the case was transferred anyway. Later that summer, Dillon described being alarmed by another new ICE tactic as the agency filed thousands of boilerplate motions to re-calendar cases in immigration court that had previously been administratively closed. Many of the cases had been administratively closed – essentially pausing removal proceedings – because USCIS, rather than the Immigration Court, had initial jurisdiction over the pending asylum applications. Some of those cases involved unaccompanied minors, according to the lawsuit, and Dillon denied two government motions to reopen such cases. “For unaccompanied minors, they have a statutory right under the law to have their asylum case decided in the first instance by the asylum office,” Dillon said. The situation came to a head in August of last year. According to the lawsuit, ICE agents arrested a young man who came to the U.S. as an unaccompanied minor after a hearing in Dillon’s courtroom, telling the judge he would be placed in expedited removal. “I had concerns because, first of all, people who are in that position cannot be put into expedited removal,” Dillon said. Protestors clashed with federal agents as they took the young man from the courthouse and Dillon said she could hear the commotion from her chambers. That afternoon, Dillon’s lawsuit alleges she emailed her supervisor warning of possible legal and due process violations, adding that courthouse ICE arrests – which had become common by then – were disrupting “the orderly administration of justice.” Dillon said she was fired by email two days later by the acting director of the Executive Office for Immigration Review. Dillon described being terminated as “really scary” – especially since it would leave her family of four without health insurance. But she said she has no regrets about sending the email. “I don’t,” Dillon said. “Like, not at all. I felt that it was my duty to bring forward something that I felt was a violation of the law.” Nearly a year after her firing, Dillon sued the DOJ, EOIR and Attorney General Todd Blanche, alleging a host of civil violations, including retaliation and violations of the Whistleblower Protection Act. “I felt it was important for people like Judge Dillon to know that they had legal recourse and they had support,” said Melanie Proctor, Dillon’s attorney. “Federal employees have a right and a responsibility to raise suspected violations of the law to the appropriate authorities within their agencies.” In an emailed statement, a DOJ spokesperson said the agency doesn’t usually comment on pending litigation or personnel matters but described the allegations in the lawsuit as “patently false.” “After four years of the Biden Administration forcing Immigration Courts to implement a de facto amnesty for hundreds of thousands of aliens, this Department of Justice is restoring integrity to our immigration system,” the agency added. San Francisco’s immigration court was officially closed earlier this month following a wave of firings and retirements involving the court’s judges. Most of the court’s cases were reassigned to the immigration court in Concord. “I think if you go back and you look at Project 2025, that’s essentially a plan that you can see happening in real time right now,” Dillon said. “They consider the immigration courts to be sort of an obstruction to a project to detain and deport as many people as possible.” For the immigrants with pending cases in immigration court, Dillon said the stakes are high. “For people who are seeking asylum, it’s about making a decision as to whether they should be returned to a country that they’re saying that they face persecution and potentially even death in that country,” Dillon said. “I think that we all have an interest in seeing that those cases are heard and decided fairly because these are people that we know and that we interact with on a daily basis.” This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: 49ers rout Rams 27-7 in NFL's first Australia game behind Purdy's 3 TDs
headlines.description: Mike Evans, Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel caught touchdown passes from Brock Purdy, and the San Francisco 49ers routed the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 Friday in the first NFL regular-season game in Australia. Purdy passed for 205 yards against the Rams’ ineffective defense at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in front of 100,021 fans, the seventh-largest regular season crowd in NFL history. Australia’s sporting capital reveled in its first real taste of American football — and in a dominant win by the 49ers, who had already won many Aussies’ affection by traveling to Melbourne a week earlier than the Rams, who only boomeranged in on Thursday morning. A party atmosphere prevailed even with a Friday morning kickoff necessary to hit the lucrative primetime television audiences in the U.S. The fans got another memorable chapter in this NFC West rivalry as the 49ers blasted the preseason Super Bowl favorite Rams with superior play on both sides of the ball. Kyren Williams scored the NFL’s first Australian touchdown on a 5-yard rush to begin the second quarter. but the Rams were a disaster Down Under. Los Angeles hadn’t lost by more than seven points since November 2024. While Purdy’s offense managed enough big plays to win, the San Francisco defense frustrated NFL MVP Matthew Stafford into a 15-of-25 performance for just 155 yards. The Niners held the NFL’s best offense last season to one score, even stopping Stafford on a fourth-down quarterback sneak from the San Francisco 1 in the third quarter. Reigning AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett was practically invisible in his Rams debut after missing much of training camp with aches, recording zero tackles. Much of the pregame talk for this trip centered around the teams’ starkly differing methods of preparation: The 49ers ingratiated themselves to the local fans as their body clocks adjusted, while the Rams stayed home until less than two days before kickoff, keeping their body clocks on California time. Both teams started with understandable sluggishness for a 10:35 a.m. kickoff, but Williams’ TD run finally got the crowd cheering. The quarterbacks then traded interceptions before Purdy shook off a shaky start and found former Rams receiver Robinson on a 39-yard post route. San Francisco surged out of halftime, with Samuel’s 45-yard kickoff return leading to Evans’ TD catch over new Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson. The Rams drove deep into the red zone, but after Puka Nacua was ruled down inches outside the goal line, the 49ers stuffed Stafford. Up next The 49ers host Miami on Sunday, Sept. 20. The Rams host the New York Giants on Monday, Sept. 21.

headlines.title: Palo Alto interfaith peace picnic continues tradition of remembering 9/11
headlines.description: In Palo Alto Thursday night, more than one hundred community members and faith leaders gathered at King Plaza to mark the 25th anniversary of the attacks on Sept. 11, 2001. This annual event honors the lives lost and changed forever on 9/11 while also leaning on the community to build a better future. This event was orchestrated by Palo Alto resident Samina Sundas, who is the founding executive director of American Muslim Voice Foundation. Sundas explained that the event started in the immediate aftermath of 9/11 as a candlelit vigil and has expanded in the years since. “And the reason we are dedicated to doing this is because we think that if we get to know our neighbors, our colleagues, then we can just build peace,” Sundas noted. At this peace picnic, attendees ate together and reflected on their memories of 9/11. An array of local religious leaders led those gathered in prayers for peace. Rabbi Heath Watenmaker of Congregation Beth Am in Los Altos Hills said, especially on the 25th anniversary this year, “it feels particularly important to be here, be part of this interfaith program, show up for our neighbors.” Many in attendance also reflected on the division and Islamophobia that surged in the wake of the attacks. Some shared first-hand accounts of the discrimination or threats they received in the months and years following. “I remember growing up in a post-9/11 America, and a lot of those wounds and those pains and those traumas are still ever-present in our community,” noted Musa Tariq with the San Francisco Bay Area Chapter of the Council on American Islamic Relations. Some attendees remembered where they were on 9/11 vividly. Others, including some teens in attendance, had not been born when the attacks happened and are learning more about the history. “The hope would be that by gathering together in community, it reminds us that we are all connected to each other and we can build a better world together,” said Reverend Dr. Eileen Altman, Associate Pastor of First Congregational Church of Palo Alto, UCC.

headlines.title: Woman arrested after viral video shows hate-motivated incident in San Jose
headlines.description: The woman at the center of a viral video where she appears to approach a father and his child to make discriminatory remarks was arrested, San Jose police said on Thursday. Police said the woman was arrested and booked into Santa Clara County Main Jail on suspicion of stalking, hate crimes and in connection with other charges. Police said officers responded to a report of a hate-motivated incident in the 6400 block of Aspen Creek on Sunday. According to authorities, the suspect approached a father and his child in her vehicle multiple times and made discriminatory remarks at them. San Jose police said Automated License Plate Reader cameras were used to identify the associated vehicle and suspect. Officials said it was also discovered the suspect was responsible for various other incidents in San Jose, including an incident at a high school located in South San Jose on Wednesday. Those incidents led San Jose Unified to send out an alert to its community on Thursday, warning them of the woman and stating she has harassed members of the community, including recording videos and posting them on social media. “We want to make you aware of a situation affecting several of our school communities. We have received reports of an individual harassing members of our community, including recording videos and taking photographs, and posting content on social media,” the district wrote. San Jose police said the investigation is active and ongoing and asks anyone with information on these cases to contact SJPD Assaults Unit Detectives at 408-277-4161.

headlines.title: Can child predators at schools be stopped before there's a victim?
headlines.description: From a longtime elementary teacher in San Mateo County to a principal in Costa Mesa, several California school employees have been arrested for child sexual misconduct charges just in the past month. Can child predators working in schools be stopped before they strike? New technology has been adopted by 12 school districts in California, including the Bay Area, aimed at doing just that, according to business owner Steve Hummel. His new software scans school-issued devices and school district networks to detect alerts of inappropriate files, like child porn. Hummel has spent the past four decades as a private investigator helping to remove dozens of dangerous individuals from classrooms. He was about to retire five years ago when he thought of the idea of creating his business, NetPropriate. “When I started noticing that there was inappropriate content that could have been discovered before there was a victim, that just started to irritate me,” he said. Hummel hired software engineers to create the software. He launched NetPropriate late last year. NetPropriate’s Steve Hummel (right) and senior investigative reporter Candice Nguyen (left). He said the technology scans the entire computer network and is not surveillance because it doesn’t open files. Rather, it looks at the signature of the file, which is a 25-alphanumeric number called a hash. If that hash file matches any of the hash files in his company’s proprietary master database, then the system knows it’s inappropriate and puts out an alert. It is ultimately up to the school district to find out why there was an alert and decide whether to act. Hummel reached out to the NBC Bay Area Investigative Unit when he reviewed the results of those alerts since school districts started using his software. “Just in the last eight months when we started actually using the software, [there have been] about 35 different computers with inappropriate content at various districts,” Hummel said. NBC Bay Area isn’t identifying the school districts out of privacy concerns. Hummel said action has been taken against at least 10 school employees ranging from termination to criminal prosecution. In many cases, the employees resigned. He said some of those employees should never work with children. “A teacher that every day, 30 minutes before school is browsing really serious inappropriate sites. 30 minutes after they got off shift again, hundreds of sites,” he described. According to the anti-sexual violence organization called RAINN, most perpetrators who sexually abuse children and create and distribute child sexual abuse material are adults the child knows and trusts. Child sexual abuse material, or CSAM, has been declared a global crisis by the child safety non-profit THORN. Since last year, there have been over 55 million suspected CSAM files reported, according to the organization. If each file is a sheet of paper, they’d cover an entire football field 620 times. And those are just the files that’ve been found. “I can almost guarantee you that anywhere you look for child sexual abuse material, you will find it,” said Julia Cordua, THORN’s CEO. “It is the tip of the iceberg because it’s only reported when it’s found, and there’s a lot that hasn’t been found.” Hummel said, based on his decades of experience as a private investigator, sadly, there may be a lot to find in the Bay Area and across California. Steve Hummel He knows his company is not going to stop the overall problem, but he hopes it’ll give some schools a chance to get ahead of some of the cases. Candice Nguyen is the senior investigative reporter on this story. If you have a question about this report or if you have another investigation tip, email her at candice.nguyen@nbcuni.com.

headlines.title: Lanes reopen on I-580 in San Leandro following SWAT activity
headlines.description: Two people are in custody following a standoff that shut down a portion of Interstate 580 in San Leandro, the Alameda County Sheriff’s Office said. The incident was first reported at 11:25 a.m. Thursday when a deputy tried to stop a Ford Mustang for a traffic violation. Authorities said the driver failed to yield and deputies did not pursue out of an abundance of caution and concern for public safety. The suspect vehicle was later located through license plate reader technology and the sheriff’s office deployed a drone to follow. Authorities said the Mustang was later seen driving the wrong way on eastbound I-580 and crashed with another vehicle before continuing to drive away. California Highway Patrol officers in the area also attempted to stop the Mustang, which continued to drive away before the vehicle was disabled and stopped. The sheriff’s office said both occupants of the car refused to come out of the vehicle, prompting a freeway shutdown and standoff. SWAT vehicles also responded to the incident just east of the Benedict Drive offramp. “The passenger eventually exited and surrendered. The driver continued to refuse commands. A chemical irritant was deployed to gain the driver’s compliance, and the driver subsequently exited the vehicle and was taken into custody,” the sheriff’s office said. Both the driver and passenger were taken to a hospital for non-life threatening injuries, officials said, adding the driver of the other vehicle the Mustang crashed into was also transported to a nearby hospital and treated for non-life-threatening injuries. headlines.title: 49ers vs. Rams recap: Brock Purdy and Co. rout division rivals 27-7 in Australia
headlines.description: What to Know Programming note: As soon as the 49ers vs. Rams game ends, flip to NBC Sports Bay Area for “49ers Postgame Live” with Kylen Mills, Rod Brooks and Jennifer Lee Chan. The San Francisco 49ers (1-1) began their 2026 NFL season with a dominant win down under, routing the Los Angeles Rams (0-1) by a score of 27-7 in Week 1 on Thursday night at Melbourne Cricket Ground in Australia. Mike Evans showed out in his first game with the 49ers, catching six of his seven targets for 49 yards and one touchdown, while Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson each added scores of their own. Brock Purdy overcame an early interception in the first half, finishing the game having completed 25 of 34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns, the lone pick and a 105.6 passer rating. Rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling was carted to the locker room in the second quarter with what the 49ers are calling an ankle injury, and tight end Jake Tonges was ruled out with a knee injury in the same quarter. Christian McCaffrey had 10 carries for 68 yards, while his rookie backup, Kaelon Black, finished with 14 carries for 65 yards. In his return to the field, star 49ers linebacker Fred Warner led the team in total (11) and solo (5) tackles. Read below for all the game highlights, news, analysis and postgame press conferences from Melbourne Cricket Ground in East Melbourne:
headlines.source: Angelina Martin, Ali Thanawalla, Nick Avila, Will Simonds, Matt Maiocco and Jennifer Lee Chan

headlines.title: Anthropic says it blocked misuse of its AI that could have supported biological weapons
headlines.description: Anthropic said Thursday it has blocked efforts by bad actors to use its artificial intelligence models for malicious activity such as cyberattacks, surveillance, and research that could have led to biological weapons. As AI models grow more powerful, elaborate cyberattacks no longer require sophisticated skills and even lone individuals can create threats that would not have been possible even a year ago, Anthropic said. The company said it has added stronger safeguards in its latest models to restrict biological research that could also be used to make weapons. “The cases we share here aren’t typical misuse, but rather examples of the most notable and novel threat activity we’ve identified to date,” Anthropic said in its third report since March 2025 describing AI misuse. The report includes snippets of the malicious code and AI prompts Anthropic said it found, and urges governments and AI competitors to identify and prevent similar abuse. “We’re publishing this work because we believe we have a responsibility to disclose malicious misuse of our services. As models become increasingly capable, their risks will increase, unless AI developers and society’s defenders act to make them safer,” the company said. The lengthy report by the AI startup, which is planning an initial public offering this fall, was published two days after one of its researchers announced he’s resigning over concerns that Anthropic and its competitors are not acting responsibly in AI development. He echoed concerns raised inside and outside of the industry about the technology’s potential to elude human control. Claude was asked to support making a virus more harmful Between December 2025 and August 2026, researchers at Anthropic found misuse by actors ranging from spyware vendors and “politically motivated individuals” to state-sponsored groups spreading propaganda. Among the findings in the company’s report are unnamed actors attempting to use its models for research that could have led to biological weapons. In one instance, Anthropic said its systems blocked a request for Claude’s assistance in authoring a grant application for scientific funding. “The work discussed in the application involved gain-of-function research (that is, research that genetically alters an organism to create a new or enhanced biological property) on the chikungunya virus. This gain of function research was aimed at the virus’ transmissibility and immune evasion properties,” the report said. Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne virus that causes debilitating symptoms such as severe pain and fever. The request involved a grant proposal for research seeking to enhance mutations to make the virus progressively more harmful. While such research could “certainly” be used to develop better vaccines and treatments, Anthropic said, “it could also be used to make the pathogen more dangerous.” Artificial intelligence Sep 9 Artificial intelligence Jul 31 Anthropic says it can’t claim its models do no harm None of the cases Anthropic included in its report were found to be using its newer, more powerful Claude Fable or Mythos-class models, with the exception of one illicit distillation case that Anthropic described as “an industrial-scale, covert campaign to extract a model’s capabilities and replicate them in another model without authorization.” Anthropic said its older models, such as Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4.5, from 2025, “were well below the threshold where they could meaningfully assist a sophisticated user in carrying out dangerous biological research.” “As a result, safeguards on these models were less stringent, directed mostly at preventing access to content that might uplift novices in recreating known bioweapons,” the report said. “But for today’s models — which are capable of assisting in a range of complex scientific research tasks — the evidence is no longer certain, and we cannot make that same assurance.” Because of this, Anthropic has applied “stronger safeguards that restrict access to a wide range of dual-use biological research queries” in its more recent models, such as Claude Fable 5, the report said. As companies introduce increasingly powerful AI models, experts have called on governments to regulate the technology, rather than relying on the industry to police itself. John Thickstun, an assistant professor of computer science at Cornell University, said it is an uncomfortable position for companies like Anthropic and OpenAI to be in when they are expected to determine what is safe vs. unsafe behavior and make “value judgments at societal scale without any kind of democratic or deliberative oversight.” Report follows a researcher’s dire warning Anthropic also found groups that created hundreds of social media accounts that look like they belong to ordinary people and then posted material amplifying the same political view over the course of a week. The company outlined nine such cases it found, originating in Russia, Iran, Turkey and across the Persian Gulf, South Asia, Africa and Europe. While social media companies can detect influence operations on their platforms once posts are circulating, “we may see it on Claude while the operation is still being built.” Anthropic released this report after one of its researchers, Jacob Coxon, announced he’s resigning amid fears the company and its chief rival OpenAI “are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” Coxon’s post warned that some of his colleagues now believe AI could threaten human life by the end of the decade. But Anthropic said it has blocked each of the malicious activities it identified, used the experience to strengthen safeguards and shared information with government authorities and industry partners. “We hope that the findings in this report will help other developers recognize similar patterns on their own platforms, give governments and civil society a clearer view of how emerging threats take shape, and strengthen collective defenses,” Anthropic said.

headlines.title: BART blames heat, aging equipment for Tuesday meltdowns in Daly City
headlines.description: A BART operations official told the agency’s governing board Thursday that aging power equipment was to blame for Tuesday’s Daly City substation fire, which broke out just as BART engineers were scrambling to deal with a rash of apparent heat-related train-control system meltdowns in the same area. At a briefing of the agency’s governing board, BART Operations Manager Sylvia Lamb said hours before the fire Tuesday night, excessive heat apparently caused an air conditioning system failure at the Daly City Station. The subsequent heat buildup in the station, she said, likely explains a rash of “false occupancy” alarms. The alarms trigger when the control system senses trains bunching up close enough to pose a collision hazard. BART responded by manually switching trains and slowing speeds through the area, causing delays all day. Lamb told the board a portable HVAC system is now cooling the station while repairs are under way. Then, apparently unrelated to the false alarms, circuit breakers tripped at the station that evening. BART staff soon discovered the substation fire, which was also spotted by a driver on nearby Interstate 280. The fire created a massive disruption in Transbay service that lasted several hours. BART 19 hours ago BART Sep 9 BART Sep 8 Crews surveying the system later found a damaged 34.5-kv cable feeding power to the station, she said. The substation is designed to cut the 34.5 kv power to 1,000 volts of direct current. Lamb noted the cable, as well as the substation itself, are original equipment on the system built back in the 1970s. Lamb said the fire was likely caused by insulation failure on a single component of the substation. “This is a very clear failure due to aging electrical equipment, it is very obvious,” she said, adding that the Daly City fire was very similar to a fault-triggered fire at a traction power substation in downtown Oakland in 2024. That station was also slated to be repaired under a bond funded project. Lamb noted that about 50 of BART’s 74 traction-power substations have never been replaced and that the station in Daly City was third on of a list of top five stations for replacement. Overhauling a substation, she said, can cost about $4 million, while replacing one can cost up to $60 million. BART has money to replace one additional substation, she said, so moving up the Daly City work will delay another high priority project. Lamb noted that BART is in the process of replacing HVAC systems but did not tell the board how soon that work will be done.

headlines.title: Police investigating deadly shooting in San Jose
headlines.description: Police are investigating a deadly shooting in San Jose’s Willow Glen neighborhood. The incident was reported at 10:20 p.m. Wednesday in the area of Oak and Palm streets. When officers arrived they found a man suffering from at least one gunshot wound. Police said the victim succumbed to his injuries and was pronounced dead by medics at the scene. The San Jose Police Department’s homicide unit has taken over the investigation, which includes trying to determine the motive and circumstances surrounding the shooting. Wednesday’s incident marked San Jose’s 19th homicide of the year. San Jose 24 hours ago San Jose Sep 9 San Jose Sep 8 Anyone with information is asked to contact Detective Sergeant Varela #3638, or Detective Montoya #3644 of the San José Police Department’s Homicide Unit via email: 3638@sanjoseca.gov and/or 3644@sanjoseca.gov or at 408-277-5283. Submit crime tips and remain anonymous by using the P3TIPS mobile app, calling the tip line at 408-947-STOP, or on www.siliconvalleycrimestoppers.org. If the information you submit leads to an arrest, you are eligible for a cash reward from the Silicon Valley Crime Stoppers Program.

headlines.title: Residents escape 2-alarm fire at San Jose duplex
headlines.description: Firefighters battled a two-alarm blaze that broke out early Thursday morning at a duplex in San Jose’s Cambrian neighborhood, according to fire officials. The fire started just after 6 a.m. at a duplex in the 2900 block of Union Avenue while residents were home. Within about 10 minutes of the first 911 call, San Jose firefighters arrived, made sure everyone was out of the building and began fighting the fire. As flames began shooting through the roof, firefighters had to leave the home and battle the blaze from outside. All residents were able to get out safely, and no firefighters were injured. Despite homes being close together in the neighborhood, the fire did not spread to any other residences. Utilities at the property were secured, according to the fire department. The cause of the fire remains under investigation. Fire officials said it was also too early to determine whether the duplex had working smoke alarms.
